meta.generatedFrom: TypeScript (the parity contract — never regenerate from Rust)
meta.description: Box-Muller normals with the spare-value cache. Two floats are consumed per PAIR of normals.
notes: HIGHEST PARITY RISK IN prng.ts: uses Math.log, Math.sqrt, Math.sin and Math.cos. sqrt is IEEE-exact; log/sin/cos are libm-dependent and are where V8 and Rust may differ by an ULP.
The `|| 1e-10` guard on u means a nextFloat() of exactly +0 is replaced by 1e-10. It also fires for nothing else, since nextFloat() is never NaN.

The spare is cached on the GameRng instance and is NOT cleared by any other method, so an odd number of nextNormal() calls leaves the instance holding a value that a later nextNormal() returns without touching the PCG stream.
meta.floatEncoding: bits = raw IEEE-754 f64, big-endian, 16 uppercase hex digits. dec = shortest round-trip decimal, informational only.
meta.nanPolicy: Every NaN is recorded as 7FF8000000000000 (the pattern of Rust f64::NAN). V8 does not emit a stable NaN sign/payload, so only NaN-ness is contractual — compare NaN results with is_nan(), not with bits.
